own_solution.law: The capacitor sees Rth = R1 R2/(R1 + R2) = 2.77913 kΩ. With zero initial voltage, V(t) = Vfinal[1 - exp(-t/(Rth C))], giving t90 = Rth C ln(10). Adding parallel capacitance q replaces C by C + q.
assumptions: The stated zero initial capacitor voltage applies at switch closure, including when further capacitance is connected in parallel.
The flash unit and its battery form a separate circuit.
For the C assignments, 'the battery' refers to the divider circuit battery.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: The numeral-free controls omit the numerical value and unit required by the general variant format, although the authors explicitly disclose this departure and do not claim that these controls preserve the number and unit.
defect_reasons.other: Because the description introduces two batteries, 'the battery' in T77C0 and TC55C can refer to either circuit, making their C versus D role ambiguous without changing the answer.

notes: The governing relations, cancellation expressions, and numerical certificates are correct under the intended reading. For added capacitances of 6.2, 15, and 33 μF, the total capacitances are 28.2, 37, and 55 μF, giving 180.457, 236.770, and 351.955 ms respectively. All listed emf values are nonzero, so the fractional-voltage cancellation is valid. The explicitly claimed numerical minimal pairs T1015/TDA93 and T6164/TE837 preserve 15 μF and change the intended temporal or object attachment. I revise the severity of my locked pass-1 rendering flag: pass 2 explicitly identifies TA387 and T7FFF as deliberate numeral-free controls, rather than falsely claiming that they preserve their twins' number and unit. Their format departure therefore does not warrant a high-severity physics or claim defect. If either emf sentence refers to the flash battery, its role is D instead of C; the charging-time answer remains unchanged. No external information was consulted.
